problemText: The library added a new wing last spring_______the renovation nearly doubled the building's reading space. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: Two independent clauses need a semicolon, a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, or a period — not a comma alone.

problemText: The chef explained her philosophy in simple terms_______fresh ingredients matter more than fancy technique. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: A colon can follow a complete sentence to introduce an explanation of what came before.

problemText: My neighbor, a retired violinist_______still practices for two hours every morning. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: Nonessential information, like an appositive naming who the neighbor is, is set off by a pair of commas.

problemText: The committee reviewed dozens of proposals_______ultimately choosing the one that required the least funding. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: A participial phrase like 'ultimately choosing...' has no subject of its own, so it takes a comma, not a semicolon or period.

problemText: The new policy — announced without warning last Friday_______caught many employees off guard. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: A punctuation mark that opens a parenthetical interruption must match the mark that closes it.

problemText: A basket of apples_______ on the kitchen counter. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: Find the true subject of the sentence; ignore the prepositional phrase 'of apples.'

problemText: The coach praised the twins because_______ had improved so much over the season. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: The pronoun must match its antecedent 'the twins' in both number and case, and it must act as the subject of the clause.

problemText: Either the manager or the interns_______ responsible for locking up the store each night. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: With 'either...or,' the verb agrees with whichever subject is closer to it.

problemText: The committee_______ its decision after months of deliberation. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: A collective noun like 'committee,' acting as a single unit, takes a singular verb — notice it already pairs with 'its.'

problemText: No one worked harder on the fundraiser than_______, according to the volunteer coordinator. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: After 'than' in a comparison, use the subject pronoun that completes the implied clause: 'than she worked.'

problemText: The number of applicants who qualify for the scholarship_______ significantly since the program expanded its outreach. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: 'The number of' takes a singular verb, while 'a number of' takes a plural verb.

problemText: By the time the guests arrived, Maria_______ the entire meal. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: When one past action finished before another past action, use the past perfect: had + past participle.

problemText: Which choice most effectively completes the sentence and avoids a dangling modifier? Walking through the museum, _______
choices: the ancient sculpture immediately caught my attention.
I immediately noticed the ancient sculpture.
my attention was caught by the ancient sculpture.
it was the ancient sculpture that caught my attention.
hints: An introductory participial phrase must be followed immediately by the noun that logically performs the action — here, the person doing the walking.

problemText: Which choice most precisely conveys that the runner covered nearly the entire ten-mile distance before her ankle gave out?
choices: The runner almost finished the entire ten-mile race before her ankle gave out.
The runner finished almost the entire ten-mile race before her ankle gave out.
The almost runner finished the entire ten-mile race before her ankle gave out.
Almost, the runner finished the entire ten-mile race before her ankle gave out.
hints: Placing 'almost' directly before the word it modifies changes the sentence's precise meaning; it should modify 'the entire race,' not 'finished.'

problemText: The safety inspector recommended that the elevator_______ before the building reopened. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: Verbs like 'recommended that' trigger the subjunctive mood: use the bare base form of the verb regardless of subject.

problemText: When the researchers finally published their results, critics_______ already raised doubts about the study's methodology. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: An action completed before another past action needs the past perfect tense.

problemText: Which choice most logically completes the sentence, ensuring the opening modifier clearly describes the archivist rather than the documents? _______, the archivist carefully catalogued the fragile documents.
choices: Having been stored improperly for decades
Discovered in a forgotten basement archive
hints: Ask who or what logically performs the action described in the introductory phrase, then match it to the subject that immediately follows the comma.

problemText: Several_______ arrived late to the rehearsal because of traffic. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: No apostrophe is needed for a simple plural — an apostrophe signals possession, not just more than one.

problemText: My_______ bicycle was stolen from the garage last night. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: Add 's to a singular noun to show that one person owns something.

problemText: The company announced that_______ profits had doubled over the past year. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: 'Its' shows possession; 'it's' is a contraction of 'it is' and doesn't fit here.

problemText: Researchers are still studying how prolonged screen time might_______ children's attention spans. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: 'Affect' is usually the verb meaning 'to influence'; 'effect' is usually the noun meaning 'a result.' After a modal like 'might,' use the bare base form.

problemText: _______ research on climate adaptation, published jointly last spring, has been cited widely. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: For joint ownership of one shared thing, only the last name in the pair takes the apostrophe + s.

problemText: The award goes to the team_______ presentation most clearly addressed the judges' concerns about long-term sustainability. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
hints: 'Whose' shows possession; 'who's' is a contraction of 'who is' and doesn't fit before a noun like 'presentation.'
